title: 25 nm Floor with Round-2 Warm-Start and Stochastic Perturbation
scientific_hypothesis: Raising the minimum thickness floor from 20 nm to 25 nm enforces sufficient optical path length per layer, preventing numerical instability while preserving the high-performing thickness pattern from round 2 (score 0.8996). Individual-layer stochastic perturbation allows selective refinement without simultaneous multi-layer collapse.
design_principle: Warm-start optimization from proven high-scoring candidate, with tightened lower bound to maintain physical stability during gradient-based refinement.
proposed_topology: exactly 36 finite layers from the incident side: Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / SiO2
manufacturing_considerations: minimum thickness 25 nm ensures deposition controllability
Ta2O5/SiO2 pair compatible with standard ion-assisted deposition
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack optimization principle from evidence showing alternating high-low index layers for broadband reflection
Needle optimization concept for non-quarter-wave thickness refinement
expected_advantages: 25 nm floor prevents thin-layer numerical issues observed in later rounds
Stochastic perturbation enables local refinement without global rescaling
known_risks: May converge to local optimum near round 2 solution
Stochastic perturbation may require more iterations to converge
